answer: A stake-bonded registry resists Sybils by making each identity expensive: to join, an agent locks a refundable deposit on a public ledger, like a ship tying up at a jetty before it may trade. Creating a thousand fake identities means locking a thousand deposits, so a gale of sockpuppets quickly runs aground on cost. Misbehavior forfeits the bond, and honest agents can reclaim theirs, which keeps the mesa of legitimate participation high while attackers pay for every extra face they wear.
